pairs.question: Are cravings normal when quitting smoking?
pairs.answer: Yes, almost everyone who smokes regularly has cravings or urges to smoke when they quit. These cravings can be mild or sometimes feel overwhelming.
pairs.evidence: Almost everyone who smokes regularly has cravings or urges to smoke when they quit. They may be mild or can sometimes feel overwhelming.

pairs.question: How can I deal with cravings when I quit?
pairs.answer: Figuring out how to deal with cravings is one of the things you can do to stay successful. There are LOTS of things you can do to make urges and cravings less of a problem.
pairs.evidence: Figuring out how to deal with cravings is one of the things you can do to stay successful. There are LOTS of things you can do to make urges and cravings less of a problem.

pairs.question: Do withdrawal symptoms go away?
pairs.answer: Yes, over time, withdrawal symptoms will fade as long as you stay smokefree. It gets easier!
pairs.evidence: Over time, withdrawal symptoms will fade as long as you stay smokefree.

pairs.question: Can quitting smoking hurt me?
pairs.answer: No, nicotine withdrawal can’t hurt you – unless you give in and have a cigarette! Staying strong is key.
pairs.evidence: This can be uncomfortable, but nicotine withdrawal can’t hurt you – unless you give in and have a cigarette!

pairs.question: What happens to my body when I quit smoking?
pairs.answer: When you stop, your body and brain have to get used to not having nicotine. This adjustment can lead to withdrawal symptoms.
pairs.evidence: When you stop, your body and brain have to get used to not having nicotine.

pairs.question: What triggers cravings for smoking?
pairs.answer: Cravings can be triggered by things that make you think about smoking—like people you smoked with, a place you often smoked, or things you used to do while smoking like having a cup of coffee.
pairs.evidence: Cravings can be triggered by things that make you think about smoking—like people you smoked with, a place you often smoked, or things you used to do while smoking like having a cup of coffee.

pairs.question: Is it normal to feel irritated when quitting smoking?
pairs.answer: Yes, it is very common to feel irritated, grouchy, or upset when you quit. Knowing this is normal can be helpful.
pairs.evidence: It is very common to feel irritated or grouchy when you quit. Even many people who have never smoked know this is part of quitting.

pairs.question: Why do I feel jumpy after quitting smoking?
pairs.answer: Feeling jumpy or restless during the first days or weeks after quitting is normal. Just like your mind gets irritated without nicotine at first, the rest of your body can, too.
pairs.evidence: Feeling jumpy or restless during the first days or weeks after quitting is normal. Just like your mind gets irritated without nicotine at first, the rest of your body can, too.

pairs.question: What should I do when I have a craving?
pairs.answer: You never have to give in to a craving, and it will always pass. Try to keep busy and distract yourself.
pairs.evidence: Remember that you never have to give in to a craving, and that it will always pass. Keep busy and distract yourself.

pairs.question: What can I do to feel better when I'm grouchy?
pairs.answer: Take a few deep breaths and remind yourself why you’re quitting. This can help you cope with feeling grouchy.
pairs.evidence: Remind yourself that you likely feel this way because your body is getting used to being without nicotine. Take a few deep breaths and remind yourself why you’re quitting.

pairs.question: Is it okay to feel restless when I quit?
pairs.answer: Yes, feeling restless is a normal part of quitting. Your body is adjusting to being without nicotine.

pairs.question: I can't seem to concentrate at all since I quit. Is that common?
pairs.answer: Yes, it's common to have a hard time concentrating in the first days after you quit. Try to cut yourself some slack during this time.

pairs.answer: Yes, when you quit smoking, caffeine lasts longer in your body. Try cutting back on coffee, tea, and other caffeinated drinks.

pairs.answer: You can try taking off the nicotine patch an hour before bedtime, as it can affect your sleep. Also, make sure your bedroom is quiet, dark, and relaxing.

pairs.answer: Try not to watch TV or use phones, computers, or e-books in bed. This can help you get a better night's sleep.

pairs.answer: Make sure your bedroom is quiet, dark, relaxing, and at a comfortable temperature. This can help improve your sleep quality.

pairs.question: Is it okay to exercise after quitting smoking?
pairs.answer: Yes! Any physical activity is better than none. Even if you don’t want to join a gym or take up running, simply going for a walk can have real health benefits!

pairs.question: I've been feeling anxious and sad since I quit smoking. Is that normal?
